newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon monitors regret killing of civilian.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon monitors regret killing of civilian.

text.p: A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon expressed "deep regret" on Saturday over the killing of a Lebanese civilian in a blast in south Lebanon two days ago.

"The Monitoring Group expressed deep regret that a Lebanese civilian was tragically killed in the explosion of side bombs near the road between the villages of Froun and Kaakiet-el-Jisr on February 20, 1997," the group, comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel said in a statement.

The Lebanese delegation presented evidence that the devices, parts of which were found on the spot, were made in Israel, the group said after a 17-hour meeting in the south Lebanon coastal village of Naqoura.
However, the Israeli delegation "emphasized that Israeli forces and those cooperating with them had not activated the bomb", the statement added.
The monitors had unanimously condemned on Wednesday the Israeli shelling of February 18 which killed a Lebanese civilian woman and wounded two others.
Under an April 26 U.S.-sponsored understanding which ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon, Israel and Hizbollah are barred from targeting civilians.
Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war to oust Israeli occupation troops from a 15-km (nine miles)-wide zone in south Lebanon.
